(PER: HON'BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE MR. JUSTICE N. V. ANJARIA) Heard learned advocate Mr.
B.R. Srinivasa Gowda for the appellant-the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Board Smt Shubha M Adiga vs Dr C.L Shivakumar on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132335109/
3 (KIADB), learned Government Advocate Mr. K.S. Harish for respondent No.1 and learned advocate Mr. Ganapathi Bhat Vajrali for the private respondent No.2.
2.

entities.text: Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Board Smt Shubha M Adiga vs Dr C.L Shivakumar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The present appeal filed under Section 4 of the Karnataka High Court Act, 1961 arises out of the judgment and order dated 29.01.2024 of learned Single Judge, disposing of the writ petition by passing the following operative order, "The award passed in respect of the petitioner's land which is the subject matter of the instant writ petition is hereby set aside and respondent No.4 is directed to pass the necessary award as per the directions issued by this Court in W.P.No.11733/2023 in respect of the land of the petitioner also, which is the subject matter of the instant writ petition.

However,
the cost imposed in shall not be applicable in the instant case."

The grievance of the petitioner was that in respect of her land bearing Survey No.40/10 at Haadihosahalli village, Thymagondlu Hobli, Nelamangala Taluka, Bengaluru Rural District admeasuring 24.04 Guntas which was acquired for the purpose of KIADB, the compensation was assessed under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

However, the petitioner claimed entitlement to be given the compensation as determined under the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as 'the 2013 Act').
3.1

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The case of the petitioner was that in relation to another property bearing same number but different parcel and adjacent to the instant land, the compensation under the 2013 Act was assessed in view of the order passed by this Court in Writ Petition No.11733 of 2023.
The petitioner wanted similar treatment.

3.2 It was noted by learned Single Judge in the impugned order that learned advocate for the respondents fairly accepted that similarly situated lands were considered for payment of compensation as per the order of the Court in the aforementioned NC:
2024:KHC:51311-DB writ petition under the 2013 Act.
The order dated 31.10.2023 passed in the said Writ Petition No.11733 of 2023, which was relied on by learned Single Judge to pass the impugned order, figures on record.

4. It was pointed out by learned advocate for the private respondent No.2 herein that in the said order also, learned advocates for the respondents had no answer to the aspect that the compensation was determined under the 2013 Act in respect of the same survey number land in view of the orders passed in Writ Appeal No.890 of 2022, Writ Appeal No.892 of 2022 and other cognate appeals.
5. Noticeably, in the said case in Writ Petition No.11733 of 2023, the same survey number for its different sub-survey number was involved.

In paragraph 7 of the order passed in Writ Petition No.
11733 of 2023, following was recorded by the Court on the basis of the submission of learned advocate for the respondents, "...against decision in W.P.no.53718/2017 and connected matters, writ appeal was filed by BMRCL and same was pending consideration.
Therefore, award came to be passed under provisions of Land Acquisition Act.

He would however hasten to add that in view of judgment passed by Division Bench of this Court in NC: 2024:KHC:51311-DB W.A.no.890/2022 Smt Shubha M Adiga vs Dr C.L Shivakumar on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132335109/
4 C/w W.A.no.892/2022 and W.A.no.1070/2022, disposed of on 27.09.2023, respondents No.4 and 5 would pass fresh award by taking note of provisions of Act, 2013 and sought for disposal of writ petition accordingly."

entities.text: NC: 2024:KHC:51311-DB W.A.no.890/2022 Smt Shubha M Adiga vs Dr C.L Shivakumar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
5.1 It is to be further noted that in yet another Writ Petition No.15395 of 2022,
which was disposed of by learned Single Judge of this Court on 22.11.2022, the same survey number land was involved for its different parcel and it was treated for the purpose of compensation under 2013 Act only.

The final aspect which emerges from the facts is that the order in Writ Appeal No.892 of 2022 which provided for determination of compensation under 2013 Act in respect of the quarry land was carried before the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Special Leave Petition No.49540 of 2023 which resulted into the order dated 09.02.2024.
5.2 The order dated 09.02.2024 passed by the Apex Court reads as under, "4.
Since the petitioner has raised only legal issues, it is not necessary for the private respondents to file any counter affidavit.
5. However, the official respondents may file their counter affidavits within four weeks.
6. The prayer for stay is declined.

The prescribed Authority-cum-Collector, under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as "the 2013 Act"), is directed to continue with the proceedings to assess the compensation in accordance with the 2013 Act.
8.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: If an award has already been passed in favour of the private respondents under the 2013 Act, let the enhanced amount of compensation be deposited by the petitioner with the Reference Court.
However, the same shall not be disbursed till further orders.
9. The amount already deposited by the petitioner-Corporation may be disbursed to the land owners without prejudice to the legal rights of the parties."
5.3 It is clear from the aforesaid order that the prayer for stay was declined by the Hon'ble Supreme Court.

Not only that, the competent authority was directed to continue the proceedings to assess the compensation in accordance with the 2013 Act and the differential enhanced amount was directed to be deposited in the Reference Court.

6. In view of all the above aspects emerging in the controversy, the judgment and order of learned Single Judge whereby the compensation was directed to be assessed and determined in accordance to the provisions of the 2013 Act books no error.
The appeal is meritless and it is accordingly dismissed.
In view of the above order, the contempt petition will not survive and it is disposed of.

sentences.text: It is directed that the parties shall abide by the order which may be passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court.

It would be incumbent in law on the part of the respondent-authorities to proceed to assess the compensation under the 2013 Act expeditiously and preferably within three months and pay to the petitioner-claimant.
In view of dismissal of the petition, the interlocutory applications would not survive and they stand accordingly disposed of.
